This is a CBP ruling about a knit glove with a polyurethane dip coating. The glove is a string knit of 95% nylon and 5% polyurethane (spandex-like), with a polyurethane coating on the outer surface. It has an extended cuff of polyester fabric.

The likely heading is 6116, gloves, knitted or crocheted, impregnated, coated or covered with plastics or rubber. Subheading 6116.10 covers gloves impregnated, coated or covered with plastics or rubber. The statistical suffix is 6116.10.9500 for "other" (not seamless?). The 6116.10 breakdown is:
- 6116.10.08 – seamless gloves, of fibers, with 43 percent or more by weight of plastics or rubber
- 6116.10.13 – other, seamless gloves
- 6116.10.17 – other
- 6116.10.44 / 6116.10.45 – other, with 50% or more by weight of cotton/man-made fibers
- 6116.10.55 – other, of cotton, 6116.10.65 – of man-made fibers, 6116.10.75 – other
- 6116.10.9500 – other

The glove is a string knit, which is typically a seamless glove. The seamless categories are 6116.10.0500 and 6116.10.1300, so classification there would depend on the plastic content. A dip coating on a string knit glove is typically a "seamless" glove under 6116.10.08 if 43% or more plastics by weight, but here the weight is unknown. The more commonly cited code for seamless gloves with a dip coating is 6116.10.1700? The ruling's likely answer, given that these gloves are generally "other" with plastic coating, is 6116.10.6500, covering other gloves of man-made fibers. I'll go with 6116.10.6500.
